key_factors: Czechia's dramatic qualification via two penalty shoot-outs demonstrates mental fortitude under pressure
Patrik Schick (Leverkusen) — capable scorer against top-level defenders, unpredictable finishing range
Tomáš Souček — set-piece threat at 192cm, Kim Min-jae will be challenged aerially
3-4-2-1 system with Šulc and Provod in the half-spaces — technically sophisticated
Neither team has altitude advantage at Guadalajara (1,566m) — neutral disadvantage
South Korea's 0-4 loss to CIV reveals defensive vulnerability against direct opponents
Korea's Tae-hyeon injury doubt disrupts their three-back cohesion
reasoning: Czechia arrive battle-hardened from a playoff route that included shoot-out wins over Ireland and Denmark (#20). The Czech Lions are not here to make up the numbers — Schick, Souček, Krejčí and Kovář are high-level professionals. However, South Korea's creative quality through Kang-in Lee and Son Heung-min's motivation represent a genuine edge. We predict Korea win 2-1 but Czechia take credit: Schick scores, Souček tests Rangel, and the Leverkusen mentality keeps the Czech Lions in this until late. Czechia will not be embarrassed.
